title: What has been searched
dek: Volumes and databases worked in this archive, so that nobody repeats them. Kept for Record Atlas as much as for this site.

rows.src: Genealogia w Archiwach — USC Szubin Miasto, marriages 1874 (sygn. 141, 6/1792/0/2.2/141), scan 10, read at the image through the Loris IIIF tile server at up to 2x native
rows.what: The LEIBHOLZ x SCHMUL marriage entry of 1874, re-read letter by letter against the registrar's own capitals elsewhere on the page
rows.got: The month is DECEMBER, not November as this archive had published. The groom's mother's forename is NOT readable: the clerk's own P in the surname on the same line and his H in the birthplace twice on the page rule out both previously published readings, and the remainder is x-height minims at the 2x ceiling. The bride's father's trade and both her parents' names are on the page and were confirmed independently by an archivist.

rows.src: Genealogia w Archiwach — same volume, scan 9 (the preceding entry) and scan 11 (the last leaf)
rows.what: Letterform controls in the same hand, and whether the volume binds an alphabetical index at the back
rows.got: Scan 9 supplies the clerk's capital W in a surname and a second instance of the month word, both decisive. SCAN 11 IS A BLANK UNUSED PRINTED FORM — this volume binds no index, though it is a three-month stub of nine entries and so the weakest possible test of that.

rows.src: Archiwum Panstwowe w Bydgoszczy — USC Szubin Miasto, ALPHABETISCHES VERZEICHNIS zum Sterbe-Register 1894-1908 (sygn. 246), 103 scans, supplied by the archive as a PDF. THE LETTER L READ ENTRY BY ENTRY, all four pages, every year 1894-1911
rows.what: LEIBHOLZ, in the death index of the family's own registry office
rows.got: NO LEIBHOLZ. K ends on scan 44 and M begins on scan 49, so the slot is bracketed at both ends, and every year from 1894 to 1911 is present in the run. THE SLOT CARRIES ITS OWN CONTROL: the first entry in it is a Jewish name and another opens 1909, so the register was not omitting Jewish deaths. Note the volume is NOT alphabetical in the usual sense — within each letter the entries run BY YEAR, so it cannot be skimmed for a surname.

rows.src: Archiwum Panstwowe w Bydgoszczy — same volume, sygn. 246, the S and Sch letters: the SURNAME COLUMN ONLY read across all nine pages, not the other columns
rows.what: SCHMUL, the bride's family, in the same death index
rows.got: NO SCHMUL in the S or Sch slots. The nearest thing is SCHIMMEL, checked at magnification because a reduced image made it look like the name. Recorded as not walked because only the surname column was read.

rows.src: Findmypast — England Births & Baptisms 1538-1975, Newington in Surrey
rows.what: The parents of the WEAR at the top of this line, born about 1823 at Newington and so before civil registration
rows.got: A GROUP BAPTISM: four children of one WEAR father baptised on a single day in 1833, born across 1820-1827, two of them opened in full and both giving the same mother. Of 189 results for the forename and surname in the window, ONE is in Surrey. CAUTION RECORDED: it is an index of the register and not the register, so it carries no occupation, and the parish held a second Wear household under a distinct middle name.

rows.src: Findmypast — 1841 England, Wales & Scotland Census, Surrey, surname WEAR with variants, born 1818-1828
rows.what: The same man in his father's household, which was the other route to the same answer
rows.got: EIGHT results and NOT ONE at Newington or Walworth — Clapham, Blechingley, Dorking, Croydon and four at Lambeth. At eighteen he may have been living in as an apprentice rather than under his father's roof. The census route is recorded as tried and unhelpful; the baptism register answered instead.

rows.src: Findmypast — British Newspaper Archive, Hertfordshire titles: exact-phrase searches on an address, on a married-name death, and on a full name
rows.what: WEAR and CASTLE at Letchworth, Hitchin and Baldock
rows.got: TWO INDEPENDENT REPORTS of one 1914 wedding, in papers published two days and two towns apart, giving the day where the GRO index gives only a quarter, the chapel, the bride's own street, and the groom's regiment and the fact that he married on furlough. AND A NEGATIVE: the 1863 death sought under a maiden name is not there, because she died under her MARRIED name — the search string in this archive's own work list was wrong. Filtered to the county, three candidates, none hers; coverage control holds, since the Hitchin paper is digitised for the adjacent year.

rows.src: Trove (National Library of Australia) — newspapers and gazettes, API v3
rows.what: LUWINSKI in Australia after the 1965 emigration, LEIBHOLZ at Melbourne, and the sponsor surname at Canberra
rows.got: A 1944 NOTICE OF INTENTION placed by the man himself, giving his street and his months of residence — the latter matching an independently documented arrival to within days. A gazette naturalisation entry for the same man. A sponsor household located to a street. MOST OF THE LUWINSKI SEAM IS THE CANBERRA TIMES 1970-1987 AND CONCERNS LIVING PEOPLE, so it is recorded and not published. INSTRUMENT NOTE: Trove normalises spelling and two spellings of one surname return an identical set.

rows.src: Findmypast — Passenger Lists Leaving UK 1890-1960 (TNA BT 27), PAGE IMAGES read, not transcripts
rows.what: The last address in the United Kingdom, which the transcript does not carry, for the April 1939 departure
rows.got: Column 6 read at native resolution for the whole page, about 30 households. The surname's own line gives 18 Ridge Ave, Letchworth, and the occupation reads Machine minder where the index has Machine minister. NO OTHER HERTFORDSHIRE ADDRESS ON THE PAGE. Page 6 of 11; the other ten pages were NOT read.

rows.src: Findmypast — Passenger Lists Leaving UK 1890-1960 (TNA BT 27), PAGE IMAGES read, not transcripts
rows.what: The same column for the August 1939 departure, as an independent check on the April reading
rows.got: Same address four months later, one brace over a woman and four children, and S Africa entered as country of intended future permanent residence. ONE Hertfordshire address elsewhere on the page (Harpenden), recorded as a fact and not as a connection. Page 7 of 15; the other fourteen pages were NOT read. NOTE FOR THE SET: BT 27 in 1939 HAS NO DESTINATION-ADDRESS COLUMN, so it cannot say where in a destination country anyone was going.

rows.src: Findmypast — Passenger Lists Leaving UK 1890-1960 (TNA BT 27), FORM REVISIONS sampled across three eras
rows.what: Which columns BT 27 actually carries, and in which years — a holdings question, not a family one
rows.got: THREE REVISIONS, AND THE USEFUL COLUMN EXISTS IN ONLY ONE OF THEM. 1907 (Walmer Castle): NO last-UK-address column at all — ages bucketed by nationality, and ports contracted to land. 1937 and 1939 (form P.M. 21): columns 1-9, WITH last address in the United Kingdom, and ending at country of intended future permanent residence — a country and nothing finer, so no destination address. 1951 (a typed US military transport manifest filed inside BT 27): ITEM/NAME/RANK/SER.NO./STATUS/DESTINATION, nothing of the Board of Trade form left. THE SERIES IS NOT HOMOGENEOUS: a column present in one piece proves nothing about another, and the era must be checked before a row is planned around a field.

rows.src: Findmypast — Passenger Lists Leaving UK 1890-1960 (TNA BT 27), PAGE IMAGE read, not transcript
rows.what: The last UK address on the 1937 departure, to test whether the 1939 address was already the family home
rows.got: Same house as both 1939 voyages, twenty-nine months earlier, and the street written out in full where the 1939 entries abbreviate it. Opened only because the form survey had just shown the 1937 sheet is the same P.M. 21 revision and therefore carries column (6) at all. The page was NOT walked — the target row was read, not every household on it.

rows.src: Landesarchiv Berlin — enquiry answered by an archivist, with scans
rows.what: A death entry, a marriage entry and a birth entry, for one Berlin family
rows.got: TWO OF THREE ANSWERED, FREE OF CHARGE, WITH SCANS. Standesamt Wedding Sterberegister 1943 (P Rep. 830 Nr. 114) and Standesamt Schöneberg II Heiratsregister 1924 (P Rep. 161 Nr. 171) — note the NAMENSVERZEICHNIS to the latter is a different shelfmark, Nr. 271. HOLDINGS FACTS WORTH CARRYING: 1912 birth registers are NOT digitised, but the NAMENSVERZEICHNISSE are; there are 150+ registry offices with NO NAME INDEX ACROSS THEM, each office indexing births, marriages and deaths separately for every year, so an enquiry without the responsible Standesamt cannot be answered at all; and the public search system CANNOT DISPLAY UMLAUTS — search an office on the stem (‘Neuk’) and pick the mangled entry from the list. Sammelakten exist alongside the marriage registers and may hold banns papers; they are not digitised and are ordered for a fee through service.berlin.de/dienstleistung/352800/.

rows.src: Landesarchiv Berlin — Sammelakte to Standesamt Schöneberg II Heiratsregister 1924
rows.what: Whether the banns file survives, and whether it holds the parties’ birth certificates
rows.got: CONFIRMED BY THE ARCHIVIST TO EXIST AND TO CONTAIN ONLY THE 1923 AUFGEBOTSUNTERLAGEN — the banns papers — AND NO DIVORCE PAPERS. Not digitised. Recorded as a positive holdings fact and a bounded negative: anyone ordering this file for divorce material will get none, and the judgment (Landgericht Berlin 251. R. 80. 40) sits in a court series instead.

rows.src: Landesarchiv Berlin LABSA — Standesamt Kreuzberg, Namensverzeichnisse zum Sterberegister
rows.what: A surname in the death indexes of one Berlin registry office, 1983-1994
rows.got: TWELVE VOLUMES (P Rep. 510 Nr. 743, 762, 781, 800, 819, 838, 920, 1066, 1184, 1284, 1456, 1471) READ PAGE BY PAGE. ELEVEN ARE A VALID NEGATIVE; ONE IS NOT, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS THE POINT. THE 1983 VOLUME IS HANDWRITTEN AND ITS OCR LAYER IS BLIND -- across 211 pages it yields 6 Schmidt, 4 Mueller and 0 Becker, 0.095 control names a page, against 1.272 for the 1984 volume. The series changes to a TYPED index at 1984 and the file drops from 125 MB to 33 MB with it. ANY NEGATIVE TAKEN FROM A LABSA TEXT LAYER MUST BE SCORED AGAINST COMMON SURNAMES FIRST; the 'Durchsuchbares PDF durch OCR-Texterkennung' label is not a promise about the names.

rows.src: Landesarchiv Berlin LABSA — Standesamt Reinickendorf, Namensverzeichnisse zum Sterberegister
rows.what: A surname in the death indexes of one Berlin registry office, 1982-1994
rows.got: THIRTEEN VOLUMES (P Rep. 130 Nr. 1478-1490) READ PAGE BY PAGE, all thirteen typewritten and legible (0.93 to 1.75 control names a page). ONE ENTRY OF THE SURNAME SOUGHT, confirmed at the image: Sterberegister Reinickendorf 1988 Nr. 2306, 5 November 1988, evangelisch. With the 1974-1981 run read in September this office is now covered without a gap for twenty-one consecutive years.

rows.src: Landesarchiv Berlin LABSA — Standesamt Spandau I, Namensverzeichnisse zum Sterberegister
rows.what: A surname in the death indexes of one Berlin registry office, 1983-1994
rows.got: TWELVE SINGLE-YEAR VOLUMES READ PAGE BY PAGE, all legible (1.26 to 1.96 control names a page). TWO ENTRIES OF THE SURNAME SOUGHT: Sterberegister 1985 Nr. 2926 (24 November 1985, ev., widowed), confirmed at the image; and 1993 Nr. 2047 (29 August 1993), a woman entered under both her birth and married names. A THIRTEENTH VOLUME, P Rep. 480 Nr. 2458 covering 1982-1986, IS BLIND (0.03 control names a page) AND IS RECORDED AS UNREAD, NOT AS A NEGATIVE. METHOD NOTE WORTH CARRYING: the 1993 volume's text layer lists names and register numbers as two unlinked blocks; positional pairing was validated across 2,396 distinct (forenames, date) keys, of which 2,394 resolve to exactly one number, and separately by the index's own practice of entering a married woman twice.

rows.src: Landesarchiv Berlin LABSA — Standesamt Neukölln, Namensverzeichnisse zum Sterberegister
rows.what: A surname in the death indexes of one Berlin registry office, 1967-1992
rows.pages: all pages of 10 volumes, plus the L block of 2 more at the image
rows.got: TWELVE VOLUMES, THE OFFICE COMPLETE FROM 1967 TO 1992, AND THE SURNAME IS IN NONE OF THEM. Ten were read by text layer; TWO CARRY NO TEXT LAYER AT ALL and were read at the image. TWO WARNINGS FOR ANYONE FOLLOWING. (1) P Rep. 380 Nr. 710 (1967-68) IS NOT ALPHABETICAL INSIDE EACH LETTER -- entries run by MONTH AND DATE -- so a nearest-name-either-side bracket proves nothing there and the whole letter must be read. (2) P Rep. 380 Nr. 822 (1985-87) IS SCANNED MIRRORED on every page and must be flipped to be read, holds THREE SEPARATE ALPHABETS (one per year), and ITS PAGES ARE OUT OF SEQUENCE -- one L block reads 252, 251, 254, 253, 256, 255, 258, 257, with the surnames chaining unbroken across all eight.

rows.src: Landesarchiv Berlin LABSA — Standesamt Kreuzberg, Namensverzeichnisse zum Sterberegister
rows.what: A surname in every spelling in the death indexes of one Berlin registry office, 1938-1979, and then four of its blind years read at the image
rows.pages: all pages of 45 volumes by text layer; L block at the image in 4 of them — 1959 pp.144-156, 1960 pp.117-130, 1961 pp.118-128, 1962 pp.118-129
rows.got: FORTY-FIVE VOLUMES 1938-1979 SCANNED AND FOUR BLIND YEARS READ PAGE BY PAGE, AND THE OFFICE IS NOW COMPLETE 1938-1994. THE TEXT LAYER OF THIS SERIES BEGINS AT 1963: seventeen volumes legible, twenty-eight blind, which was measured rather than assumed and contradicted a prediction that all forty-five would be blind. The reading produced TWO PEOPLE in fifty-seven years — a 1948 death and a 1960 death — and the 1960 one carries a NINTH SPELLING OF THE SURNAME that no index or search engine would have matched, read off the registrar's own hand at five times magnification. TWO THINGS WORTH CARRYING AWAY. (1) The L block sits at 40-48 per cent of the way through every Kreuzberg volume of this era, so the band is found in one render rather than hunted. (2) A SILENT BLIND VOLUME IS NOT A NEGATIVE: every volume here was scored against six common surnames before its silence was believed, and the four that mattered were read by eye instead.

rows.src: Zentral- und Landesbibliothek Berlin — Berliner Adressbuch, Namenteil, annual volumes
rows.what: One surname's householder runs read at the page image, 1939, 1941, 1942 and 1943, to match a memorial book's boroughs to printed households
rows.got: A REPLICATION THAT PAID FOR ITSELF, AND A LESSON ABOUT READING A DIRECTORY RUN. The four runs were read at the image and agree entry for entry with a reading made three weeks earlier, which is what established that the task waiting on them had never needed waiting on. THREE THINGS FOR ANYONE READING FRAKTUR DIRECTORY RUNS. (1) These pages are FOUR COLUMNS WIDE and the ink profile will not show the gutters, because the column rules are printed lines and score as ink; estimate the columns from the text block's width instead. (2) A RUN CAN SPLIT ACROSS A COLUMN BREAK AND THE HEADWORD IS REPEATED at the top of the next column, so a run that looks short at the foot of a column is not short. One of these four also repeats the headword MID-COLUMN after a single entry. (3) THE PER-PAGE OCR CAN INTERLEAVE TWO ADJACENT COLUMNS LINE BY LINE AND SAY NOTHING ABOUT IT: in the 1941 volume it attributed nine entries of the NEXT SURNAME to this one, which a search-based method cannot detect and an alphabetical check at the image catches at once. Reading the run in place in the full page text works for three of the four volumes; it is wrong, silently, for the fourth.

rows.src: Geneteka (Polskie Towarzystwo Genealogiczne) — province pomorskie, 11pm
rows.what: Four surnames across births, marriages and deaths in one Polish province, with the coverage of eleven named towns tested and Jewish-surname controls run
rows.pages: whole-province exact-match queries plus two parishes enumerated in full (Debrzno rid 1568, Przechlewo rid 890) and one measured by era (Chojnice rid 194)
rows.got: RECORDED AS BLOCKED, NOT AS NOTHING, AND THE CONTROL IS WHY. GENETEKA'S POMORSKIE HOLDING CONTAINS ESSENTIALLY NO JEWISH RECORDS: province-wide births give SCHMIDT 1,134, KOWALSKI 1,023 and MÜLLER 767 against COHN 1, LEVY 0, LEVIN 0, ISRAEL 1, JACOBSOHN 2 and ROSENTHAL 3. It is an index of Catholic and Protestant parish books, so a Jewish surname's zero here is evidence about the index and not about the family, and anyone recording such a zero as a negative is recording a false one. THE COVERAGE BOUND IS THE SECOND HALF. Of eleven former German towns tested by name, NINE ARE NOT INDEXED AT ALL — including Człuchów (Schlochau) and Czarne (Hammerstein), where a place search returns two other towns of the same name in other provinces and neither is the right one. The two that are indexed stop early: Przechlewo holds 1,457 births ALL BEFORE 1800 and Debrzno (Preussisch Friedland) 1,649 births ALL BEFORE 1840, while the province indexes 1874-1925 perfectly well elsewhere. Chojnice (Konitz) is the exception and runs to 1939 with 6,107 births. THE SITE'S SEARCH IS AN AJAX CALL: the HTML page returns an empty table and the rows come from api/getAct.php as JSON, capped at fifty per request; api/getParish.php?search=<place> answers the coverage question directly and is the first call worth making. The province code is POSITIONAL and an invalid one falls back silently to dolnośląskie, which has produced a false zero in this archive before.
